extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing to submit manuscripts to BMC Neurology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting manuscripts (research articles, reviews, case reports, software, databases, protocols, etc.) to the BMC Neurology journal, including formatting, data and file requirements, licensing, fees, and peer review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal; BMC Neurology is an open access, peer-reviewed journal that considers articles on all aspects of the prevention, diagnosis and management of neurological disorders and related molecular genetics, pathophysiology, and epidemiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal welcomes manuscripts in specified neurology areas (neurodegenerative diseases, cerebrovascular disorders, epilepsy, headache, neuroinflammatory conditions, neuromuscular diseases, movement disorders, cognitive and behavioral neurology, infectious diseases of the nervous system, genetic/molecular basis, clinical trials, neuroepidemiology, diagnostic biomarkers and neuroimaging, preventive strategies). As a BMC Series journal, editorial decisions are not based on perceived interest/impact: manuscripts are considered for publication if they are scientifically valid. For research articles this includes having a clearly defined and sound research question, appropriate methodology and analysis, and adherence to community-agreed standards relevant to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Processing Charge (APC) and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: An article processing charge (APC) applies for each article accepted for publication; the current APC for BMC Neurology is £2390.00 GBP / $3190.00 USD / €2690.00 EUR (subject to VAT/local taxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APC price is determined from acceptance date. Springer Nature operates a country-tiered APC pricing pilot (check APC applicable to your country). Funding options: institutional agreements, funder/institutional open access funding, APC waivers and discounts for corresponding authors based in the world's lowest income countries, and discretionary waivers for financial need (requests must be made at submission; requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered). Visit open access support portal and Journal pricing FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and copyright (Creative Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC Neurology articles are published open access under CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY licences; under Creative Commons licences authors retain copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY-NC-ND: share for non-commercial purposes with attribution; permission needed for commercial re-use or derivatives. CC BY: may be shared and adapted for any purpose, including commercially, with attribution. Authors may seek licence variations to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: General style and formatting: use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; embed special characters; do not use page breaks in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all special characters are embedded in the text to avoid loss during conversion to PDF. Do not use page breaks; follow specific article-type formatting guidelines in addition to these general points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable file formats for main manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Editable files are required for processing: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich Text Format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-editable files (e.g., PDFs) are submitted, you will be required to re-submit an editable file when submitting a revision or after acceptance. For TeX/LaTeX users, use Springer Nature LaTeX template; a PDF will be compiled using pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021. All relevant editable source files must be uploaded during submission; failing to do so will delay production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged or required to provide all datasets on which conclusions rely, either by depositing in public repositories or presenting them in the paper/additional files; data should be machine-readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where community expectation exists for data archiving, deposition in a community-endorsed public repository is mandatory. Include an 'Availability of data and materials' section with the required format: e.g. "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink...]." If data are included as additional files, use the specified phrase. BioMed Central endorses Force11 Data Citation Principles and requires all publicly available datasets be fully referenced with accession numbers or DOIs. For databases and software, include repository web/ftp address, project name, archived version DOI, operating systems, programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing the 'Availability of data and materials' section (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific required phrasing for data availability statements depending on where/how data are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When data are in a repository: include repository name and unique persistent identifier/hyperlink. When data are included as additional files: state that the datasets are included within the article (and its additional file(s)). For databases, state the web/ftp address and any restrictions to use by non-academics.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: what to cite
rubrics_metrics.description: Only cite articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or that are available through public e-print/preprint servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list but may be mentioned in text as "unpublished observations" or "personal communications" with names; obtain permission to quote personal communications. Journal abbreviations follow Index Medicus/MEDLINE. Any in-press articles necessary for reviewers' assessment should be made available if requested. Use reference management software to ensure correct formatting and check the Instructions for Authors for the relevant article type for style examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: web links and URLs formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: All web links and URLs, including authors' own websites, should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details including title, URL and date accessed. If an author/group can be clearly associated with a web link, include them. Example format provided in guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure preparation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order they are first mentioned and uploaded in that order; multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file; figures must be uploaded in correct orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) in the main manuscript (not in the graphic file). Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic. Closely crop figures to minimise whitespace. Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB. Design figures to be legible at final web/PDF sizes (web: 600px standard/1200px high-res; PDF: widths 85 mm or 170 mm; max height 225 mm). Image resolution ~300 dpi at final size; all lines >0.25 pt at standard widths; embed all fonts. File types accepted: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word (single page), PowerPoint (single page), TIFF, JPEG (photographs), PNG, BMP, CDX. Vector figures: prefer PDF. TIFF: save with LZW compression. JPEG: save at maximum quality. Minimise conversions between file types. Obtain permission to reproduce previously published figures; indicate permission in figure legend and include original source in references. Contact info@biomedcentral.com for figure queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table preparation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in sequence; tables less than one A4/Letter page can be placed within the manuscript; larger tables at the end or as additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger datasets or wide tables can be uploaded as additional files (Excel or CSV). Table titles (max 15 words) above the table and legends (max 300 words) below. Do not embed tables as figures or spreadsheet files; use the 'Table object' function. Color and shading may not be used; highlight parts via superscript/numbering/lettering/symbols or bold with explanations in the legend. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values. Contact info@biomedcentral.com for table queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: content, naming, size and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may provide datasets, tables, movies, or other supporting information as additional files; all additional files will be published with the accepted article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised main manuscripts with tracked changes as additional files (send by email if requested). Results otherwise noted as 'data not shown' should be included as additional files. Do not link to data on personal/departmental websites. Maximum file size 20 MB each; files will be virus-scanned. Each additional file should be cited in sequence in the main text and named 'Additional file 1' etc. Provide in the manuscript a separate section listing file name, file format, title, and description. Use standard file extensions. See 'How to use additional files' for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must include: an explanation of why your manuscript should be published in BMC Neurology, explanation of any issues relating to journal policies, declaration of potential competing interests, confirmation that all authors have approved submission, and confirmation the content has not been published or submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any additional information requested for your specific article type. If submitting to a special issue, refer to its specific name in the covering letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting or excluding peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cover letter, authors may suggest potential peer reviewers and may enter details of anyone they prefer not to review the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional email addresses where possible, or identifiers (ORCID, Scopus ID) to help editors verify reviewer identity. Intentionally falsifying reviewer information (e.g., false name/email) will result in rejection and possible investigation under the misconduct policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting your work in well-written English improves chances that editors and reviewers will understand and evaluate it fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help options: watch English language tutorial, ask a native speaker colleague, or use professional language editing services (Springer Nature Author Services offers English language improvement, scientific in-depth editing, table formatting, manuscript formatting, specialist translation). A free language quality check via partner AJE is available. Using such services is not required and does not guarantee selection for peer review or acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review evaluates the quality of a manuscript before publication by independent researchers in the field; typically two or more experts evaluate manuscripts based on scientific robustness, originality, and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' feedback guides editors' decisions; editors may consult editorial board members. BMC Neurology operates transparent peer review: if published, reviewer reports are published online under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 but reviewers are not named. Reviewers and editors must declare competing interests and can be excluded if a competing interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer (Transfer Desk) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is not accepted in the chosen journal, a transfer to a different journal within the Springer Nature portfolio may be offered to authors; transfers allow resubmission of manuscript files and reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: choice of alternative journals, no reformatting necessary, save time. Transfer Desk combines author preferences and editor recommendations with journal-matching technology. Transfers are not completed without the author's input; authors can decline or withdraw a transfer at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and database article metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For software articles include project name, project home page, archived version DOI, operating system(s), programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear metadata (examples given) to ensure reproducibility and accessibility; follow specific article-type pages for further mandatory information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables previously published elsewhere, especially if the original was not open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission should be indicated in the figure legend and the original source included in the reference list. Ensure permissions cover open access publication if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission by authors only (no third-party submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitting user is an author; follow journal submission system rules.
